items.title: Preoperative transthoracic echocardiogram and delay to geriatric hip fracture surgery.
items.abstract: Delays to surgery confer increased morbidity and mortality in elderly patients who have sustained hip fractures. Preoperative investigations including transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) are often requested. The aim of this study was to determine whether there were delays to surgery when these patients underwent preoperative TTE. Electronic databases were searched from inception until April 2025. All relevant studies were identified with data extracted and meta-analysed. A total cohort of 2,581 patients was extracted from 5 studies; 865 (34%) patients received a preoperative TTE, and 1,716 (66%) patients did not. Baseline characteristics of age, sex, fracture pattern and treatment were similar. Patients receiving a preoperative TTE were more likely to have coronary artery disease (CAD), congestive cardiac failure (CCF) and arrythmia. The mean time to surgery was 9.4h ( p = 0.09) shorter in the group not receiving a TTE. The mean length of hospital stay was 0.6 days ( p = 0.03) shorter in those who did not receive a preoperative TTE. The available evidence did not demonstrate a statistically significant association between time to surgery and preoperative TTE. However, the data available are limited by heterogeneity, confounding and insufficient statistical power. In general, improving access to, and efficiency in TTE could help minimise delays to surgery, particularly in centres with limited resources. Strict adherence to American College of Cardiology guidelines for preoperative TTE indications is recommended.
items.journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England

items.title: Enoxaparin dose assessment in paediatric cardiology patients.
items.abstract: Enoxaparin is a commonly utilized anticoagulant, particularly in infants and children. Recent literature has highlighted the need to initiate enoxaparin at higher doses, especially at younger ages, due to differences in pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. The aim of this study was to investigate the enoxaparin dose required to achieve therapeutic effect in patients ≤ 2 months, >2 to ≤ 6 months, >6 to ≤ 12 months, and >12 months old. This retrospective chart review includes patients aged 0-18 years admitted to the cardiac ICU or cardiac stepdown unit over a five-year period. Patients were included who achieved a therapeutic anti-Xa within goal of 0.5-1 units/mL. Seventy-one patients were included in the analysis; 26 (37%) were ≤ 2 months old, 21 (30%) were >2 to ≤ 6 months old, 10 (14%) were >6 to ≤12 months old, and 14 (20%) were >12 months old. There was a significant difference in the median enoxaparin dose required among these age groups, with medians of 2.13 mg/kg/dose [IQR: 1.95, 2.53], 1.81 mg/kg/dose [IQR: 1.52, 2.40], 1.44 mg/kg/dose [IQR: 1.31, 1.71], and 1.16 mg/kg/dose [IQR: 1.00, 1.26], respectively (p 12 months of age, despite higher initial doses in patients ≤ 6 months old. Infants admitted to the cardiac ICU or cardiac stepdown unit required an increased median enoxaparin dose and a higher number of dosing changes and experienced longer times to achieve therapeutic anti-Xa levels compared to older children.

items.title: Short- and long-term outcomes of balloon pulmonary valvuloplasty in children ≤24 months with critical and haemodynamically significant pulmonary valve stenosis: a 20-year single-centre experience in Medellín, Colombia.
items.abstract: Balloon pulmonary valvuloplasty is the treatment of choice for critical and haemodynamically significant pulmonary stenosis, but long-term outcome data in infants, particularly in Latin America, remain limited. We evaluated long-term outcomes and factors associated with adverse outcomes in children ≤24 months. We retrospectively included consecutive patients ≤24 months who underwent balloon pulmonary valvuloplasty for critical or haemodynamically significant pulmonary stenosis between January 2004 and July 2024. Outcomes included significant restenosis, moderate-or-greater pulmonary regurgitation, pulmonary valve reintervention, and surgical reintervention. Time-to-event outcomes and predictors were assessed using Kaplan-Meier estimates and Cox regression. A total of 129 patients were included (median age 1.5 months; 37.2% with critical pulmonary stenosis). Procedural success was 94.5%. The median right ventricular-to-pulmonary artery gradient decreased from 44 to 7 mmHg ( p Z -score was associated with a lower hazard of restenosis. Ballon pulmonary valvuloplasty is a safe and effective first-line therapy in children ≤24 months, providing sustained haemodynamic improvement and durable long-term outcomes. Patients requiring predilation, larger balloon-to-annulus ratios, or having smaller pulmonary annulus Z -scores may benefit from closer long-term echocardiographic surveillance.

items.title: A Nanodelivery Platform Harnessing Synthetic Lethality and Efferocytosis Inhibition for Synergistically Enhanced Immunotherapy of Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
items.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), defined by the absence of specific therapeutic targets, shows poor clinical benefit and readily develops chemoresistance, underscoring the need for therapies that couple precise tumor cell killing with robust antitumor immunity. Drug-induced immunogenic cell death (ICD) is a promising approach. However, its efficacy is curtailed by limited tumor-cell targeting with collateral immune-cell damage and by overactive efferocytosis that rapidly removes ICD-associated danger signals, thereby restricting antitumor immunity. Herein, we develop a microenvironment-responsive nanocarrier co-delivering both PLK1 inhibitor (BI6727) and TIM-3 inhibitor (ML-T7). It integrates dual-bioeffect of synthetic lethal selective ICD and whole-immuno system remodelling initiated by effective macrophage efferocytosis inhibition. In detail, the molecular hallmark differences between tumor and immune cells was utilized to provide high-quality antigens. Meanwhile, the nanotherapeutic enables serial phagocyte regulations, such as, suppressed macrophage phagocytosis, enhanced antigen recognition and phagocytosis by dendritic cells (DCs), and then alleviated T cell exhaustion. The underlying mechanism of nanotherapeutics-mediated overall immune system reprogramming was explored by transcriptional profile analyses. These findings indicate that precise molecularly targeted ICD combined with coordinated immune activation enables efficient primary tumor suppression and promotes T-cell phenotypes associated with antitumor immune memory, providing a novel paradigm for cancer immunotherapy.

items.title: Integrated Viscoelastic Microfluidics for Label-Free Separation and Concentration of Circulating Tumor Cells.
items.abstract: Developing advanced instrumentation systems for the automated, precise isolation of target circulating tumor cells (CTCs) from blood, followed by molecular marker analysis, stands as a pivotal trend in the field of liquid biopsy. However, current isolation technologies typically rely on subsequent centrifugation steps to enrich CTC samples for downstream assays, such as single-cell western blotting (scWB), creating challenges for developing integrated systems. Here, we present an integrated viscoelastic microfluidic system (IVEM) that leverages viscoelastic fluids to automatically separate and concentrate CTCs. The IVEM includes a CTC separation module (CSM) for high-purity isolation and a CTC concentration module (CCM) to remove excess cell suspension. To clarify the working mechanism, particle migration behavior is systematically analyzed through theoretical modeling and numerical simulations and validated by polystyrene (PS) particle experiments. The performance of the IVEM is evaluated through separation experiments using blood samples spiked with MCF-7 cells. The processing throughput, purity, recovery rate, and concentration factor of MCF-7 cells reach 1.82 mL·h-1, 82.13 ± 2.87, 81.30 ± 4.72, and 4.26 ± 0.92%, respectively. The IVEM enables label-free, continuous on-chip enrichment of separated CTCs without additional off-chip processing. This integration facilitates future incorporation of other functional modules, such as high performance single-cell capture, into liquid biopsy systems, thereby further enhancing the clinical applicability of technologies such as scWB.

items.title: Biomarkers of subclinical cholestasis predict cancer immunotherapy outcomes.
items.abstract: In a recent paper published in Cancer Cell, we identified subclinical cholestasis as an accessible imprint of gut dysbiosis predicting resistance to immune checkpoint blockade. Our work connects γ -glutamyl transferase, bile-acid remodeling, and MAdCAM-1 loss to compromised antitumor immunity, opening avenues for novel biomarker-guided microbiota interventions.

items.title: Reprogramming tumor cells with LCOR mRNA nanotherapy to enhance immunotherapy.
items.abstract: Transcription factors (TFs) are often considered undruggable due to their structural complexity. mRNA technologies can overcome this therapeutic limitation by enabling dynamic protein replacement therapies. Here, we explore the TF activity of LCOR (Ligand-dependent corepressor), which suppresses tumor growth, at least in part by inducing the antigen presentation machinery (APM) in tumor cells and constraining cellular plasticity. These effects facilitate tumor immune recognition and immune-mediated tumor eradication. We used poly β-(amino esters) (pBAE) nanoparticles (NPs) for local delivery of Lcor mRNA in multiple breast cancer models. pBAE-NPs efficiently encapsulate mRNA and facilitate cellular uptake, achieving optimal endosomal escape, resulting in high transfection efficiency in vitro and in vivo, restoring LCOR function in tumor cells and engaging their APM. In preclinical models, intratumoral delivery of Lcor mRNA reduced tumor growth. Importantly, the combination of Lcor mRNA-loaded RH-pBAE-NPs with anti-PDL1 or anti-CTLA4 immunotherapies eradicated most of the tumors in our preclinical TNBC model. Overall, our nanotherapeutic strategy emerges as an innovative TF-replacement therapy in a lock-in/wipe-out fashion, leveraging the immunogenic effects of LCOR to eradicate breast cancer tumors when combined with immunotherapy.

items.title: RNA-Binding Proteins Regulate CD8 + T Cell Biology: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Opportunities.
items.abstract: Immune-related diseases contribute substantially to global morbidity and mortality. CD8 + T cells play a critical role in adaptive immunity by eliminating virus-infected and malignant cells. The biology of CD8 + T cells is governed by tightly regulated gene expression programs, and disruption of these programs can lead to diverse immunopathologies and malignancies. This article evaluates our current understanding of post-transcriptional and translational regulation of gene expression in CD8 + T cells by RNA-binding proteins. Relevant and up-to-date literature was critically analysed to gain mechanistic insights into the roles of RNA-binding proteins in CD8 + T cell biology and to identify key knowledge gaps and future directions, with particular emphasis on therapeutic implications. RNA-binding proteins regulate diverse aspects of CD8 + T cell biology, including differentiation, cytokine production, stress adaptation and proliferation. Recent studies further reveal how dysregulated expression and function of RNA-binding proteins contribute to hyperinflammation and haematological malignancies. RNA-binding proteins are emerging as key post-transcriptional and translational checkpoint regulators of CD8 + T cell biology and represent promising therapeutic targets for immune-related diseases; however, substantial mechanistic and disease-specific studies, as well as rigorous translational validation, are required before RNA-binding protein-targeted therapeutic strategies can be safely and effectively advanced into clinical practice.

items.title: Multimodal assessment of exceptional responders refines subtyping-directed precision treatment in HR+/HER2- breast cancer.
items.abstract: BACKGROUNDWe previously defined 4 hormone receptor+/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2- (HR+/HER2-) subtypes: SNF1 canonical luminal, SNF2 immunogenic, SNF3 proliferative, and SNF4 RTK driven. The FASCINATE-N proof-of-concept trial demonstrated that subtyping-directed precision treatment improves pathologic complete response in locally advanced HR+/HER2- breast cancer, yet efficacy remains suboptimal.METHODSWe integrated transcriptomic, genomic, digital pathology, and clinical data from this trial (n = 230) and focused on exceptional responders to explore opportunities for refining treatment strategies.RESULTSIn SNF1, we uncovered that perineural invasion diminished endocrine therapy efficacy, suggesting the potential benefit of incorporating perineural blockade. Digital pathology and spatial transcriptomics identified that the spatial architecture of the tumor-stromal-immune interface influenced apatinib efficacy in SNF4, highlighting the importance of interfering with the tumor microenvironment. In the SNF3 group, exceptionally well responders exhibited multiple mutations in DNA repair genes and cell cycle activation, correlating with the efficacy of poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase and CDK4/6 inhibitors. Additionally, we illustrated that lymphatic vessel infiltration was linked to improved immunotherapy outcomes in HR+/HER2- SNF2 tumors.CONCLUSIONOverall, our study emphasizes the importance of multimodal assessments in optimizing precision treatments for HR+/HER2- breast cancer.FUNDINGNational Natural Science Foundation of China, grant numbers U25C2032, 82441028, and 82573645; The Shanghai Key Laboratory of Breast Cancer, grant number 12DZ2260100; The Human Phenome Data Center of Fudan University.TRIAL REGISTRATIONClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05582499.

items.title: Hepatitis D virus infection in persons with HIV and hepatitis B virus across Europe: A cross-sectional analysis of the HDV-Europe cohort.
items.abstract: Infection with hepatitis D virus (HDV) is known to accelerate the progression of liver disease and is associated with mortality in individuals with HIV and hepatitis B virus (HBV). However, little is known about current HDV epidemiology, including HDV-testing practices and prevalence, in this population in Europe. We conducted a cross-sectional study of clinical cohorts across Europe (Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland, Spain, Switzerland and United Kingdom). Included individuals were those living with HIV, ever hepatitis B surface antigen positive, aged ≥18 years and actively in care on December 31, 2023. We calculated the percentage of individuals tested for HDV, prevalence of individuals who ever had anti-HDV positive serology (i.e., past/current infection) and the prevalence of individuals whose last HDV RNA result was positive (i.e., active infection). A total of 2970 individuals were included. Anti-HDV antibody results were available in 2189 (73.7%). Of them, 261 (12.0%) had past/current HDV infection, ranging between 3.8% in the United Kingdom and 27.3% in Poland. Among the 261 individuals with an anti-HDV-positive result, 162 (62.1%) had been tested for HDV RNA. Of them, 92 (56.8%) had active HDV infection. Of the overall population with available data, active HDV infection was observed in 4.4% (n = 92/2077), ranging between 0.9% in the Netherlands and 11.0% in Italy. In Europe, about one-eighth of individuals with HIV/HBV in care have evidence of past/current HDV infection, in whom half have active HDV infection. Nevertheless, these results come from a setting where one-quarter have yet to be tested for anti-HDV antibodies.

items.title: Letter to the Editor Regarding "BEAT-B Study (Behavior, Aspirations, and Treatment Needs): A Mixed-Methods Study of Patient Values, Preferences, and Barriers to Care Among People Living With Chronic Hepatitis B in South and Southeast Asia".
Hepatitis A-Associated Very Severe Aplastic Anemia in a Young Adult Female: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Hepatitis‑associated aplastic anemia (HAAA) is a rare but life‑threatening immune‑mediated complication of acute viral hepatitis, and hepatitis A virus is an uncommon cause of this syndrome. We report the case of a 24‑year‑old woman who developed acute hepatitis A followed by rapidly progressive pancytopenia fulfilling the criteria for very severe aplastic anemia. Her clinical course was complicated by febrile neutropenia, transfusion dependence, gastrointestinal bleeding, and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia bacteremia. Bone marrow biopsy demonstrated marked hypocellularity with severe trilineage suppression. Despite intensive supportive care including broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy and transfusion support, her clinical condition deteriorated, and she died from infectious and hemorrhagic complications before definitive therapy could be initiated. This case emphasizes the importance of early recognition of cytopenias during the acute phase of hepatitis and prompt hematology referral for definitive management. Aplastic anemia following acute hepatitis A infection is rare but potentially fatal. Early recognition of cytopenias during or following acute hepatitis, prompt bone marrow evaluation, and urgent hematology referral is essential for timely definitive treatment and improved outcomes.

items.title: Multi-omics analysis explores the potential mechanisms of Huangtcia renifolia ethanolic extract against osteoporosis in ovariectomized rats.
items.abstract: Huangtcia renifolia (L.) H. Ohashi & K. Ohashi, a traditional folk medicine, has been used for centuries by the Dai people in Xishuangbanna, Yunnan Province, China. Traditionally, it has been used to clear kidney heat, promote diuresis, and treat conditions, including kidney deficiency, sexual dysfunction, hepatitis, and osteoporosis. Recent pharmacological investigations indicate that Huangtcia renifolia ethanol extract (DRS) exerts bone-protective effects, partially via modulation of OPG/RANKL/RANK and BMP-2/Smad signaling pathways. This study used an integrated multi-omics strategy to explore the bone-protective effects of DRS and its potential mechanisms in ovariectomized (OVX) rats. The chemical composition of DRS was profiled by widely targeted UPLC-MS/MS. Osteoporosis was induced in rats via bilateral ovariectomy, and bone status was assessed using serum biochemical analyses, micro-computed tomography (microCT) and hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) staining of femur tissue. Integrated multi-omics analyses were subsequently performed, comprising 16S rRNA sequencing of fecal microbiota, widely targeted serum metabolomics, and femoral transcriptomic sequencing. In vitro validation was performed using MC3T3-E1 osteoblasts treated with DRS-containing serum. DRS treatment significantly increased bone mineral density, improved trabecular bone microstructure, and effectively reversed abnormal bone turnover markers in OVX rats. Gut microbiota profiling indicated that DRS treatment modulated the gut microbiota, with significant increases in the relative abundance of Lactobacillus and Limosilactobacillus . Serum metabolomics identified 34 metabolites differentially abundant in DRS-treated rats, with pathway enrichment analyses highlighting purine metabolism as one of the principal affected pathways. Femoral transcriptomics and RT-qPCR validation indicated that DRS treatment was associated with upregulation of osteogenic genes ( Col1a1 and Col1a2 ) and downregulation of muscle-related genes ( Myog , Myh3 , and Mstn ), consistent with potential modulation of pathways linking bone and muscle function. Additionally, DRS-containing serum dose-dependently enhanced osteoblast differentiation and upregulated BMP2 and RUNX2 expression in vitro . DRS treatment protects against osteoporosis in OVX rats. This protection was associated with gut microbiota composition, serum metabolic profiles, and the expression balance between osteogenic and muscle-related genes in bone.

items.title: Etiology Dependent Differences in Immunotherapy Response and Prognosis Between MASH-HCC and HBV-HCC.
items.abstract: The incidence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis related hepatocellular carcinoma is increasing. However, its response to immunotherapy remains unclear. This study aimed to compare the prognosis of patients with MASH-HCC and hepatitis B virus-related HCC (HBV-HCC) under different treatment strategies. This single-center retrospective study included 218 patients with HCC from 2022 to 2025. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS), and the secondary endpoint was 1-year overall survival (OS). Kaplan-Meier analysis, Cox regression models, and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis were used to evaluate the association between immune cells and prognosis. Stratified and subgroup analyses were also performed. A total of 136 HBV-HCC and 82 MASH-HCC patients were enrolled in this study. PFS was significantly longer in HBV-HCC patients than in MASH-HCC patients (70.59% vs 41.46%, P P overall=0.036). Stratification by CD4⁺ T-cell cutoff (354 cells/μL) showed that the prognostic gap between etiologies was diminished in patients with higher CD4⁺ T cell levels, while lower CD4⁺ T cell counts were associated with poorer PFS in MASH-HCC. MASH-HCC patients showed a trend toward poorer response to ICI therapy compared with HBV-HCC patients, particularly in those with CD4⁺ T cell counts <354 cells/μL. These results suggest that both disease etiology and immune status may contribute to variability in immunotherapy outcomes and warrant consideration in treatment decision making.

items.title: Graph attention network-driven single-cell omics analysis reveals how B4GALNT1-mediated glycosylation remodelling of the ferroptosis-pyroptosis network promotes drug resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma.
items.abstract: Acquired resistance to sorafenib in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is accompanied by coordinated changes in oxidative-stress handling and regulated cell-death pathways, yet how membrane organisation connects these adaptations is not fully resolved. We therefore examined whether B4GALNT1, a ganglioside biosynthetic glycosyltransferase, couples changes in ganglioside composition and lipid-raft architecture to ferroptosis regulation and caspase-1/GSDMD-associated signalling in sorafenib-resistant HCC. We combined TCGA-LIHC analysis, single-cell transcriptomics, pathway-level analyses, and graph attention network modelling with a treatment-annotated local cohort of 92 patients with HCC who received sorafenib. Functional experiments were conducted in Huh7/Huh7-SR cells and additional liver-tumour models using B4GALNT1 gain- and loss-of-function, an independent second-sgRNA knockout clone, GM1 rescue, and re-expression of either wild-type B4GALNT1 or the catalytic-loss D358A variant. Validation included ganglioside profiling, detergent-resistant membrane isolation, lipid-raft disruption/repletion, ferroptosis-directed pharmacology, cell-death measurements, and xenograft studies. B4GALNT1 was enriched in tumour-associated hepatocyte populations and was upregulated in Huh7-SR cells. In the local cohort, higher B4GALNT1 protein abundance tracked with less favourable response to sorafenib and poorer survival outcomes. Increasing B4GALNT1 shifted ganglioside abundance toward GM2/GM1/GD2 and increased GM1-enriched raft-associated fractions, whereas knockout produced reciprocal changes. B4GALNT1-high cells showed increased GPX4 and SLC7A11, reduced lipid peroxidation and labile Fe 2 + , and lower ferroptotic injury. At the same time, caspase-1/GSDMD-associated signalling and IL-1β/IL-18 release increased without widespread terminal membrane lysis. Exogenous GM1 partially rescued knockout-associated changes, and wild-type B4GALNT1 restored the phenotype more effectively than the D358A mutant. Concordant directional effects were observed in additional cell models and in xenografts. The data are consistent with a model in which B4GALNT1 reshapes ganglioside composition and GM1-enriched membrane microdomains, thereby supporting a drug-adapted state that combines greater ferroptosis resistance with restricted caspase-1/GSDMD-associated membrane permeabilisation. This integrated phenotype accompanies reduced sorafenib responsiveness and offers a mechanistic basis for acquired resistance in HCC. B4GALNT1 is associated with sorafenib resistance and poorer outcomes in treated HCC. B4GALNT1 remodels gangliosides and lipid rafts, limiting ferroptotic injury. Caspase-1/GSDMD signalling increases without widespread terminal membrane lysis. Genetic rescue and cross-model studies support B4GALNT1 specificity.

items.title: ATF6-mediated GTPase RHOQ promotes liver cancer progression via enhancing aerobic glycolysis through PAK1 phosphorylation.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) ranks among the most prevalent malignant tumours worldwide, accounting for approximately 90% of primary liver cancer cases, with the highest incidence observed in Asia. Activating Transcription Factor 6 (ATF6) is an endoplasmic reticulum stress-responsive transcription factor. Our previous studies have demonstrated that ATF6 contributes to HCC tumourigenesis and progression through signalling pathways such as ATF6-CTH-Keap1-mTORC1 and ATF6-PPM1H-RPS6KB1. RNA sequencing identified ATF6 transcriptional targets, with Ras homolog family member Q (RHOQ) validation via chromatin immunoprecipitation and electrophoretic mobility shift assay. RHOQ expression and clinical significance were analysed in HCC cohorts. Functional assays assessed proliferation, migration, invasion and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Tumour growth was evaluated in orthotopic (NOG mice) and subcutaneous (nude mice) models. Mechanistic analyses were performed to characterise RHOQ-mediated regulation of p21-activated kinase 1 (PAK1) signalling and metabolic remodelling. Furthermore, therapeutic synergy between PAK1 inhibitor IPA-3 and Glypican-3 (GPC3)-CAR T cells was tested. We identified RHOQ as a direct transcriptional target of ATF6. Clinically, elevated RHOQ expression correlated with poorer progression-free survival (PFS) in patients with HCC. Functionally, RHOQ promoted the proliferation and metastasis of liver tumour cells. Correspondingly, RHOQ knockdown markedly suppressed tumour growth in xenograft models, with consistent results observed in a hydrodynamic tail vein injection(HTVi) model. Mechanistic investigations revealed that RHOQ directly bound to PAK1, promoted its phosphorylation and activation and thereby drove aerobic glycolysis in liver tumour cells. Furthermore, combined treatment with the PAK1-specific inhibitor IPA-3 and GPC3-targeted CAR T-cell therapy produced a significant synergistic anti-tumour effect. In summary, this study systematically delineated the importance of the ATF6-RHOQ-PAK1 signalling cascade in driving liver cancer progression and provided a rationale for the design of targeted combination therapies. RHOQ is a novel direct transcriptional target of ATF6 in HCC. High RHOQ expression is associated with unfavourable clinicopathological features and poorer PFS. RHOQ drives HCC progression via PAK1 activation and aerobic glycolysis. Combining the PAK1-specific inhibitor IPA-3 with GPC3-targeted CAR T-cell therapy produces a potent synergistic anti-tumour effect.

items.title: Efficacy and Safety of Low-Dose Hypofractionated Radiotherapy Combined with Immunotherapy for Liver Metastases: A Single-Center Retrospective Analysis.
items.abstract: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of low-dose hypofractionated radiotherapy (LDHRT) for liver metastases when combined with immunotherapy. Patients with liver metastases receiving immunotherapy were enrolled in this study at Changzhou Second People's Hospital from January 2019 to May 2025 (Ethics Approval No. [2021]KY117-01). LDHRT (12 Gy in 3 fractions) was administered to the liver metastases using volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT). The tumor response was evaluated according to the RECIST 1.1 standard. Clinical and imaging data were collected to assess changes in tumors inside and outside the radiation field before and after LDHRT, as well as the median progression-free survival (PFS) for lesions within the radiation field. A total of 51 patients were included, with the median age of 69 (range 47-84) years; 86.3% (44/51) were male, and 94.1% (48/51) had an ECOG performance status (PS) score ≥1. Additionally, 54.9% (28/51) had received ≥3 lines of prior therapy. Due to the continuous progression of liver metastases under systemic treatment, LDHRT was administered for the liver metastases. The study found a high local control rate within the radiation field as the objective response rate (ORR) and disease control rate (DCR) within the radiation field were 17.6% and 86.3%, respectively. However, the efficacy for lesions outside the radiation field was significantly inferior, with an ORR of 0% and a DCR of 35.3%. The median PFS for lesions within the radiation field was 4.23 months. Patients with colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) showed better PFS than those with gastric cancer liver metastases (GCLM). The most common adverse events were fatigue (16/51, 31.4%), abnormal liver function (11/51, 21.6%), and hypothyroidism (7/51, 13.7%). No patients discontinued treatment due to treatment-related adverse events. LDHRT combined with immunotherapy provided favorable local control and was generally well tolerated in patients with liver metastases. No apparent abscopal effect was observed, suggesting that single-lesion LDHRT was insufficient to reverse systemic immunosuppression.

items.title: Clinical outcomes after interstitial high-dose-rate brachytherapy vs. stereotactic body radiotherapy in hepatocellular carcinoma: A retrospective matched single-center analysis.
items.abstract: Interstitial high-dose-rate brachytherapy (iBT) and stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) are local treatment options for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Data comparing their efficiency and safety profile remain limited. Therefore, we aimed to compare treatment results of iBT and SBRT in HCC patients. Patients with HCC who underwent iBT or SBRT between 2014 and 2024 at our tertiary center were retrospectively analyzed. Local control (LC), progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS) were evaluated. Treatment-related acute and chronic toxicities were assessed. In a cohort of 92 patients with 125 HCC lesions, 60 patients (65.2%) with 86 lesions (68.8%) were treated with iBT. The median follow-up was 21 months. There were no significant differences in LC ( p = 0.73) or PFS ( p = 0.27) between iBT and SBRT cohorts. To reduce confounding due to imbalances in baseline characteristics, a 1 : 1 matched sub-cohort was generated. For all patients with complete clinical data, each SBRT patient was matched to one iBT patient using a multivariable distance metric based on Charlson comorbidity index (CCI), liver cirrhosis, Child-Pugh score (CPS), albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) score, and age, resulting in two equally-sized groups with reduced baseline imbalance. After matching, the OS advantage of iBT over SBRT was no longer statistically significant. The most common acute treatment-related toxicities were grade 1 elevations of liver enzymes in the iBT group (12/60, 20%) and fatigue in the SBRT group (5/32, 15.6%). In the iBT group, two minor bleeding events and one pneumothorax occurred, but no grade > 3 late toxicity was observed. Both iBT and SBRT provide effective local treatment options for HCC, achieving comparable LC and PFS, while maintaining a manageable toxicity profile. Patient selection should be guided by institutional expertise and patient preference.

items.title: Association of the Platelet-to-Neutrophil Ratio With Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Liver Fibrosis in U.S. Adults: NHANES 2017-March 2020.
items.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a chronic liver disease that is not related to alcohol and is characterized by excessive accumulation of fat within liver cells. As one of the most common chronic liver diseases worldwide, MASLD affects about a quarter of the world's population and is expected to become a leading indication for liver transplantation by 2030. The disease not only increases the risk of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, but also is closely associated with a variety of extra-hepatic complications such as type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease. Although many biomarkers such as N-terminal type III collagen propeptide (PRO-C3), enhanced liver fibrosis (ELF), and Fibrosis-4 Score (FIB-4) have been used to identify and predict MASLD and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), their clinical utility remains limited. Recent studies have shown that neutrophils and platelets play a crucial role in the progression of MASLD. The platelet-to-neutrophil ratio (PNR), a novel biomarker, has shown predictive value in ovarian cancer and myocardial infarction. However, PNR has not been fully studied in MASLD. The aim of this study was to investigate the association between PNR and MASLD and to explore its relationship with hepatic steatosis and fibrosis. This cross-sectional study included participants from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic dataset. Hepatic steatosis was defined as a controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) ≥ 274 dB/m, and MASLD was defined as hepatic steatosis plus at least one cardiometabolic criterion according to the 2023 multisociety steatotic liver disease (SLD) nomenclature. Advanced liver fibrosis was defined as a liver stiffness measurement (LSM) ≥ 8.2 kPa. PNR was calculated as the platelet count divided by the neutrophil count and log2-transformed (log2-PNR). Missing covariates were handled by multiple imputation ( m  = 20). Survey-weighted logistic regression, natural-spline smoothing, threshold effect analysis, and subgroup analyses were used to evaluate the association between log2-PNR and MASLD. A total of 3437 adults aged 18 years and older were included (mean age 47.5 ± 17.5 years; 48.1% male). In the fully adjusted model, higher log2-PNR was inversely associated with MASLD (OR 0.75 per doubling of PNR, 95% CI 0.63-0.90), and with hepatic steatosis; participants in the highest PNR quartile had lower odds of MASLD than those in the lowest quartile. Threshold effect analysis identified a breakpoint at PNR approximately 38 for MASLD, with a significant nonlinear pattern. Higher log2-PNR was also inversely associated with advanced fibrosis (OR 0.43, 95% CI 0.33-0.57), with no significant nonlinearity. Subgroup analyses showed that the inverse association was more pronounced in males and non-Hispanic White participants for MASLD (P for interaction = 0.009 and 0.037, respectively). Higher log2-PNR was inversely associated with the cross-sectional presence of MASLD and hepatic steatosis, and with advanced liver fibrosis, in U.S. adults. Log2-PNR, an easily obtained inflammatory marker, is independently associated with MASLD. These findings require validation in prospective cohort studies.
